answer: Make every identity the sole custodian of a unique random data shard: at enrollment the network assigns each account a sable-dark block of data that only it must store and serve. Spot-checks demand a proof of retrievability within seconds, so a shard cannot be fetched from a shared pool on demand. At the zenith of activity, a Sybil operator with a hundred identities must keep a hundred shards online at once, like a knoll that grows with every fake — disk, bandwidth, and uptime costs scale linearly and cannot be amortized, because no two identities share the same shard or the same check.
